newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak says news on disposals soon.
newsitem.headline: Malbak says news on disposals soon.

text.p: South Africa's Malbak Ltd said on Wednesday it would make an announcement soon on plans to sell its unlisted units, but declined to comment on reports it might sell Defy to Electrolux.
"We will be putting out a statement," acting chief executive Peter Beningfield told Reuters.
"I had hoped to do it towards the end of this week but it will probably be next week because I want to tie up a few loose ends."
Beningfield said the company remained on schedule to make a distribution to shareholders by the end of March or early April.
Swedish appliance maker Electrolux said earlier on Wednesday that it was considering the purchase of Malbak's unlisted Defy unit, which makes white goods.
"The company is for sale as far as we know and we are looking at it," Electrolux deputy managing director Lennart Ribohn told Reuters on Stockholm.
Swedish business daily Dagens Industri said Electrolux had placed a bid for Defy believed to be worth between 320 and 480 million crowns (200 to 300 million rand).
But Beningfield declined to be drawn on the report, stating: "I'm not going to comment on anybody we might be talking to."
The disposals by Malbak of its unlisted subsidiaries form part of the group's decision to unbundle its assets in a bid to unlock the value of its underlying investments.
In terms of listed investments Malbak has decided to distribute the shares it owns in these to shareholders.
Malbak said last week that unlisted subsidiary Eagle Freight had secured German firm Thyssen Haniel Logistic GMbH as a 35 percent stakeholder.

Current Eagle Freight management bought the firm for an undisclosed sum which the company says was over 50 million rand, but has now sold 35 percent of the group to Thyssen Haniel Logistic, which is the transport and logistics arm of conglomerate Thyssen AG

Beningfield said in December the sale of three of its unlisted units, Eagle Freight, Stalcor and Tedelex would generate more than 120 million rand. Malbak has previously stated that the proceeds from the disposal of all the unlisted units was expected to exceed 700 million rand.
Other unlisted companies include Malbak Motor Holdings, ICL (SA) and Amalgamated Appliances.
Listed companies in which Malbak has a major stake include Foodcorp, Kohler, South African Druggists, Ellerine and New Clicks.

Exchange control regulations inhibit the sale of Malbak's 64 percent stake in London-listed MY Holdings Plc. But MY said last week it would welcome any decision to distribute its stake in some way among Malbak shareholders.
